title: serving-runtime-daily-scratchpad-2026-03-08
content:
2026-03-08 - quick scratchpad

Morning check-in:
- p99 spikes on canary after rolling 2026-03-07 22:00 UTC. Reported by Jin.
- Repro steps (local): loadtest small-batch (seq_len 512) -> backend A -> NVLink saturation -> request queueing -> p99 ~850ms (baseline ~320ms).

Top-of-head triage items:
1) SRV-1423: unexpected serialization delay in KV cache flush path. Affects canary and any model with caching enabled. Severity: p2 (regression for cached workloads).
   - Repro: run repro script in /bench/repro/srv-1423.sh (needs large prefix and interleaved requests).
   - Hypothesis: atomic write ordering + mutex contention when cache eviction coincides with writeback.
   - Next: instrument lock hold times (add scoped timers) + add a stress test to CI. Owner: Asha.

2) Kernel fallback on A100 after driver bump (PR #378). Symptoms: occasional fallback to reference aten kernel for attention (slower).
   - Theory: cudnn/cuBLAS version mismatch triggers slower path.
   - Action: ask infra to try driver 535.x on a small node pool, run full attention microbench. Owner: Jin.

3) Serving runtime memory leak (suspected) on model-x-1.2. Observed increase in GPU mem over 8 hours.
   - Quick-check: run perf spec with memory-tracking build (env TRACK_ALLOC=1).
   - If positive, isolate between KV cache and allocator. Owner: Liam.

Perf TODOs (short list):
- Run batch-size sweep for model-x for seq_len [128,256,512,1024] on dedicated-2 GPUs. Collect tokens/s and tail latency. (ASAP)
- Add a benchmark that exercises prefix-cache + streaming to catch serialization ordering regressions. (blocked by SRV-1423 fix)
- Try quantized attention kernel from PR branch qkernel/attn-quantv2 — compare throughput and accuracy delta on sample prompts.
- Re-run nightly perf job with new kernel-selection policy (flag enable_kernel_probe=true) and capture which kernels are selected.

Kernel notes / experiments:
- Observed that attention kernel selection prefers tiled-gemm for seq_len <= 256 but falls back to generic for longer sequences; might be wrong threshold. Need to add adaptive threshold that takes GPU SM occupancy into account.
- Work item: implement small probe at model load that runs microbench on a tiny input (cold-start cost small) and caches results in model metadata. Could avoid repeated fallback.

Immediate checkpoints for today:
- [ ] Add lock timers + flush stress test for SRV-1423 (branch: fix/srv-1423-lock-timers).
- [ ] Coordinate with infra about driver test (request ticket sent).
- [ ] Start batch-sweep experiments and upload results to /bench/results/2026-03-08/ (csv + short notes).
- [ ] Post short summary to #serving-runtime once we have initial repro and metrics.

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- If lock timers show >50% time in eviction path, consider converting to RCU-like approach or defer writeback to dedicated worker.
- Could use per-model eviction queues to avoid global contention. But watch memory blow-up.
- Consider adding a metric: eviction_wait_seconds (histogram) to alert on regressions.

Links / refs:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/378 (driver bump + build changes)
- Jira: SRV-1423 (KV cache flush contention)
- Local repro: bench/repro/srv-1423.sh

End-of-day quick log: keep this as scratchpad — move notes to Confluence if we need a formal postmortem.
